source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 27 April 1933, p. 16 ("Down local elections: Castlereagh")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: the nine names and their divisions read from the News-Letter's Castlereagh nomination list (27 April 1933, p. 16), which states 'There will be no contests for the nine seats'

note: Triennial election of the nine rural district councillors, one for each electoral division. Nominations closed on 26 April 1933 and, there being no contest in any division, the nine nominees were returned unopposed. Polling in County Down took place on 25 May 1933. Filed on 1933-05-25, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1933-06-01 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Small. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Holywood' to Holywood Rural (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Castlereagh Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-45 name the DED Holywood Rural; the rounds were filed as Holywood (rural) (1924); Holywood Rural (1927, 1930, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958, 1961, 1964, 1967); Holywood (1933); Holywood (Rural) (1936). This round was filed as 'Holywood', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (holywood) answers with a redirect to this one.
